name: variant_b

name: r1-archetype-audit
finding: Human review of .evolve/ideas/variant_b.json: all 12 'promotable' candidates are 2-layer capability co-occurrence pairs (bundle-X-Y format), not archetypes. All have identical judge scores (utility=0.8, novelty=0.8). Real archetypes encode (prompt pattern, family binding, measurable recall lift) — these encode only (capA, capB). The R1 judge rubric passed anything above a low threshold.
action: Do NOT merge these to registry/. Use the candidate set as negative training examples for R2 judges — teach them that capability co-occurrence ≠ archetype.
implication: R2 proposers' judgeAgreementRate target against this set is now different: correlation with 'NOT promotable' is the right signal for these 12, not correlation with 'promotable'. Proposers D/E/F should treat this set as labeled false positives.

name: r2-converged
finding: Both measured variants (D, E) flat at ideasaiRecall 0.878. Neither regressed held-out. The ceiling at 0.878 is architectural — the planner's auto-attach system ships tailwind+shadcn+industry, and the 3-layer expected lists in corpus/ideasai-prompts.json cannot be reached without changing the hot-path planner OR enriching the corpus expected lists with the auto-attached layers.
recommendations: The scaffold-side training loop is saturated. Moving the ceiling requires a real-outcome signal — exactly what blueprint-agent session events would provide. Drew asked for the spec; I provided it in-session.

Corpus expected lists should be re-labeled: add tailwind/shadcn/industry to every React SaaS expected list. This alone would jump ideasai Jaccard from 0.456 to ~0.85 with zero code changes. Cheap, honest, and unlocks meaningful measurement.
Archetype promotion from bare manifests is broken at the entity level (variant_d proved this). Real archetype promotion needs template files. This is a separate pursuit.

name: scaffold-quality-audit-r1
hypothesis: VB traces show 54% end-to-end pass rate. If we audit each framework layer locally for install+typecheck pass, we'll find the real template bugs without needing VB's scenario→spec mapping.
fix: 5 TypeScript family package.jsons were missing typescript + @types/node as devDependencies, causing pnpm exec tsc to fall back to a system tsc that doesn't understand ES2022. Added explicit typescript@^5.7.0 + @types/node@^20.0.0 to: cli-ts, electron-desktop-ts, expo-react-native-ts, fullstack-ts, tauri-desktop.
outcome: KEEP — 10.8pp pass rate gain, no regressions, 8 specific bugs isolated for follow-up

name: r3-signal-collapse
finding: R3 dispatched 2026-04-20T04:00 to build self-healing audit→fix→judge→apply pipeline against 5 remaining broken layers. Between dispatch and execution, the 5 target layers were fixed by manual structural work on PRs #9-#12 (router fix, deep-clean, planner split, React-Vite App.tsx). Full audit 2026-04-20T19:10 shows 37/37 layers pass. Coverage target met trivially; no failure signal for a proposer to train against.
audit: 37/37 framework layers pass local install+typecheck. tangle-blueprint passes audit; harness cleanup throws ENOTEMPTY on temp dir (bug in scripts/audit-scaffold-quality.mjs line 139, unrelated to scaffold quality).
implication: variant_g (rules engine) would match zero error signatures. variant_h (LLM proposer) would have no novel input to generalize over. variant_i (hybrid) has no fast-path or slow-path to exercise. Executing R3 now produces empty artifacts.
action: Do NOT build variant_{g,h,i} against zero-failure input. The auto-fixer is still the right tool to build, but it needs real failures to train against. Next governor pass should either (a) run buildout-pipeline to find fresh failures, (b) pivot to the new signal surface (template-rewrite rate from buildout-analysis.json), or (c) intentionally introduce a regression to bootstrap training data.

name: variant-A-tier1-first
hypothesis: Pre-workspace intercept: scan all registry families' tier1 keywords; if any has ≥2 distinct matches, route as single-starter instead of workspace.
finding: Mechanism works for real prompts (verified synthetically on KYC/fraud/polymarket) but metric is mechanically bounded — 26 of 54 unrouted buildout scenarios have initialPrompt:null. Router cannot route text that doesn't exist. Escalated trace-capture bug upstream.

name: variant-B-partner-first
hypothesis: When partnerGuess is explicit, treat partner as primary routing signal. Scan families matching partner via id/tags/keywords/tier1. If score≥2 on frontend/api/agent/fullstack/blueprint surface, route partner-aligned family as single-project workspace. Fall through otherwise.
finding: Partner metadata routes around the null-initialPrompt issue Variant A hit — 7 tangle-network scenarios + deno-llm-proxy gained route via partner signal even when prompt text is missing. First-pass inferPartner from text regressed 19 tests; narrowed to explicit partner only. Score≥2 threshold + surface allowlist prevent contract-lane false positives.

name: r4-converged
finding: Target exceeded 3x (0.308 vs 0.10). Variant B's partner-first routing broke the architectural ceiling evolve hit at 0 for 6 rounds. Partner metadata is a strong signal evolve couldn't exploit without structural change to the routing code path.
secondaryFinding: Variant A's null-initialPrompt discovery explains why prompt-text-based routing plateaued — even though the mechanism works on live prompts, 48% of the measurement corpus literally lacks the text needed to exercise it. This is a separate Gen 8 trace-capture fix, not an eval-gaming concession.
